description: Hands-on PC and laptop hardware: what every component does, how to choose, assemble, configure and repair a machine, and how to install and tune the operating system on it. Taught to the depth of the professional hardware technician certification, with every procedure practised on real or virtual machines.
modelledOn: CompTIA A+ Core 1 (220-1101) hardware and networking objectives
Andrews, Dark and West, CompTIA A+ Guide to IT Technical Support
outcomes: Identify every component on a motherboard and explain how CPU, chipset, memory and buses connect.
Choose and install processors, memory, storage, power supplies and expansion cards that are compatible with one another.
Configure BIOS/UEFI, boot order, secure boot and firmware updates safely.
Install and configure operating systems, drivers and printers on desktops and laptops.
Diagnose hardware faults with a repeatable troubleshooting procedure and basic tools.
Specify a custom build for a stated budget and workload, including power and thermal limits.

units.title: Safety, tools and the anatomy of a PC
topics: Electrostatic discharge, mains safety, lifting and handling; the technician toolkit
Form factors: ATX, micro-ATX, mini-ITX, SFF; case airflow
Tour of a disassembled desktop: identifying every part and cable
Documenting a system: inventory, serial numbers, photographs before disassembly

units.title: Motherboards, processors and memory
topics: Motherboard layout: sockets, chipset, VRMs, slots, headers, jumpers; reading the manual
CPU basics for technicians: cores, threads, clock, cache, TDP, integrated graphics; Intel and AMD sockets
Installing a CPU, thermal paste and coolers; air versus liquid cooling; thermal throttling
DRAM: DDR4 and DDR5, DIMM and SO-DIMM, channels, ECC, XMP/EXPO profiles; installing and testing RAM
Buses and interfaces: PCIe lanes and generations, SATA, M.2, USB versions, Thunderbolt

units.title: Storage devices and power supplies
topics: Hard disks, SATA and NVMe SSDs, flash wear, SMART data; RAID 0, 1, 5, 10
Partitioning (MBR, GPT), file systems (NTFS, FAT32, exFAT, ext4) and cloning a drive
Power supply ratings, 80 Plus efficiency, rails, connectors, modular supplies; calculating a wattage budget
Uninterruptible power supplies and surge protection for unstable mains; testing a PSU
Backup media and external storage

units.title: Expansion, peripherals and display devices
topics: Graphics cards: GPU, VRAM, outputs, power and slot requirements; installing and testing
Sound, network, capture and other expansion cards; USB and wireless peripherals
Display technologies: LCD (TN, IPS, VA), OLED, refresh rate, resolution, colour depth; projectors
Video interfaces: HDMI, DisplayPort, DVI, VGA, USB-C alt mode; multi-monitor setup and calibration
Keyboards, mice, scanners, webcams, barcode and smart-card readers; KVM switches
Connectors and cables: identifying, testing and replacing them

units.title: BIOS/UEFI, firmware and boot
topics: POST, beep and LED codes; BIOS and UEFI settings, boot order, secure boot, TPM, virtualisation flags
Firmware updates and recovery; CMOS battery and resetting settings
Boot process from firmware to bootloader to kernel; UEFI partitions
Overclocking, fan curves and power limits: what is safe

units.title: Installing operating systems
topics: Creating installation media; clean install, upgrade, image deployment
Installing Windows and a Linux distribution; dual boot and partitioning
Drivers, Windows Update and package managers; activation and licensing
Post-install tasks: user accounts, security updates, antivirus, backup, restore points
Virtual machines as a safe way to practise installations
Recovery tools: safe mode, recovery environment, bootable rescue media

units.title: Installing and configuring printers
topics: Laser, inkjet, thermal and 3D printer technologies and consumables
Local, network and wireless printer installation; drivers and print queues
Sharing a printer, print servers, printing from phones
Common faults: paper jams, streaks, blank pages, offline printers; preventive maintenance

units.title: Laptops and mobile devices
topics: Laptop anatomy: batteries, chargers, keyboards, displays, hinges, SO-DIMMs, M.2 drives
Disassembly technique and manufacturer service manuals; replacing a screen, battery and keyboard
Power management, battery health and charging circuits
Docking stations, port replicators and wireless cards; phones and tablets basics

units.title: Custom configurations
topics: Matching a build to a workload: office, gaming, CAD, video editing, virtualisation host, small server, thin client
Compatibility checking: socket, chipset, RAM, PSU, case clearance, PCIe lanes
Costing a build in cedis from local and online suppliers; import and warranty considerations
Benchmarking and burn-in testing a new machine

units.title: Troubleshooting
topics: A six-step troubleshooting method: identify, theorise, test, plan, implement, verify and document
No-power, no-POST, no-display, overheating, random reboots, blue screens, slow performance
Diagnostic tools: multimeter, POST card, memory test, disk health, stress tests, event logs
Preventive maintenance in dusty and humid conditions; cleaning and thermal servicing
Writing a repair report and talking to a non-technical user

schedule.title: Safety, form factors and a tour of the PC
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page safety checklist for a repair bench in a dusty workshop covering ESD, mains and lifting, and photograph or sketch a system before opening it.

tasks.title: Choose the correct ESD precautions and tools from a given toolkit for opening a desktop, and fix three unsafe steps in a given repair sequence
Identify and label all 14 parts and cables inside a disassembled desktop in the bench, then say what each connects to
Select a case and board form factor for three client briefs and justify each by airflow, expansion slots and space constraints

schedule.title: Motherboard, CPU and cooling
schedule.exercise: Using a motherboard manual excerpt, list the socket, chipset, memory slots and front-panel header pin layout and say what each one is for.

tasks.title: Locate the sockets, slots, headers and jumpers on a virtual ATX motherboard and match each to the connector it takes
Install a CPU, apply thermal paste and mount a cooler on a virtual board, then confirm the idle temperature stays below the throttle limit
Match three CPUs to boards by socket and chipset, rejecting incompatible pairs, and compare cores, cache and TDP for a given workload

schedule.title: Memory, buses and interfaces
schedule.exercise: Make a table comparing PCIe, SATA, M.2 and USB generations by speed and typical use, with one sentence on when to pick each.

tasks.title: Install two DDR4 DIMMs in the correct slots for dual-channel mode and confirm the detected capacity and speed
Fit an NVMe drive, a graphics card and a SATA SSD so each gets full lanes, and read the resulting link speeds from the board report
Diagnose a build with mixed DIMM speeds that boots at a lower clock, then rebuild the memory layout and enable the right profile to restore full speed

schedule.title: Storage, power and backup
schedule.exercise: Calculate a power budget for a given build and write a short note on the PSU rating, efficiency class and UPS you would specify for unstable mains.

tasks.title: Add up component wattages for a mid-range build and choose a PSU with 20 percent headroom, then check the connectors it needs
Set up four disks in RAID 0, 1, 5 and 10, then compare usable capacity and fault tolerance after failing one drive in each
Size a UPS and surge protection for a computer lab that loses mains twice a day, estimating run time on battery for the connected load

schedule.title: Expansion cards and displays
schedule.exercise: Compare an IPS, a VA and an OLED display for a school computer lab, considering viewing angle, brightness in daylight and cost.

tasks.title: Install a graphics card in a virtual build, connect its power cables and confirm it appears in the device report
Fit a network card and a sound card in free slots of a virtual desktop and fix the one that conflicts with a case slot
Choose a display for three user profiles by panel type, refresh rate and resolution, and explain the trade-off between cost and use

schedule.title: Video interfaces and peripherals
schedule.exercise: List the cables you would stock for a small repair shop and explain which connector standard each one replaces or supports.

tasks.title: Connect two monitors to a PC using HDMI and DisplayPort, then set resolution and arrangement to match a given desk layout
Set up a KVM switch with two PCs, a keyboard, a mouse and a barcode scanner, and test that every device is recognised on each PC
Test a bench of eight cables for continuity and pin faults, identify the faulty ones and replace them with the right type

schedule.title: Firmware, BIOS and boot
schedule.exercise: Write a short guide for a non-technical user explaining what happens between pressing the power button and seeing the desktop.

tasks.title: Interpret three beep or LED error codes from a virtual board and name the failed component for each
Step through the boot process from firmware to bootloader to kernel and mark where a missing boot file would stop the machine
Set a safe overclock and fan curve in firmware for a given CPU and cooler, keeping temperature under the limit while measuring the performance gain

schedule.title: Installing operating systems
schedule.exercise: Plan a dual-boot layout for a 512 GB drive with Windows and Linux, writing the partition sizes and boot order you would use.

tasks.title: Create bootable installation media steps for a lab of 20 PCs and select the right image method for clean install or deployment
Partition a virtual disk and install a Linux system alongside a second system in a dual-boot layout, then verify that both boot
Install missing drivers and updates on a fresh virtual machine, using a package manager, and confirm all devices show as working

schedule.title: Post-install hardening and recovery
schedule.exercise: Write a checklist of ten tasks you would do after installing an operating system for a small office, in priority order.

tasks.title: Create user accounts, enable updates and set a restore point on a fresh virtual machine, then restore it after a deliberate change
Build a virtual machine for practice installs, take snapshots before and after a risky change, and roll back to the clean state
Recover a virtual machine that fails to boot after a bad update, using safe mode and rescue media, and document the steps taken

schedule.title: Printers and print servers
schedule.exercise: Compare running costs of laser and inkjet printing for a school office that prints 2000 pages a month, in cedis.

tasks.title: Match laser, inkjet, thermal and 3D printers to five printing needs and list the consumables each one uses
Add a network printer to a small office network with a static address, install its driver and print a test page from two PCs
Fix a printer that shows offline for users by diagnosing address, driver and queue faults across a small network, and write what you changed

schedule.title: Laptops, batteries and mobile devices
schedule.exercise: Read a service manual excerpt and write a numbered disassembly plan for replacing a laptop keyboard, flagging the steps most likely to cause damage.

tasks.title: Identify the battery, SO-DIMM slot, M.2 drive, display cable and hinge screws in a virtual laptop teardown
Replace the screen and battery of a virtual laptop following the service manual order, without leaving any connector or screw unaccounted for
Diagnose a laptop that will not charge by testing the adapter, charging circuit and battery health, and decide whether to repair or replace

schedule.title: Specifying and building a machine
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page recommendation for a client choosing between a new PC and an upgrade, with a cost in cedis and the reasoning.

tasks.title: Check a parts list for socket, chipset, RAM, PSU and case clearance mismatches and correct the two incompatible items
Design a build for a video editing workstation within a stated budget and justify each part against the workload
Cost three builds in cedis from local and online suppliers including import duty and warranty, and recommend one in a client scenario

schedule.title: Troubleshooting method and repair report
schedule.exercise: Write a repair report for a client with a machine that randomly reboots, explaining the cause and the fix in plain language.

tasks.title: Apply the six-step troubleshooting method to a reported no-display fault in a case scenario, choosing the next step with evidence at each stage
Diagnose seven faults, such as no power, no POST, overheating and random reboots, on virtual PCs using the right tool for each
Use a multimeter reading, POST card code and memory test result together to find the single failed part in a PC with two symptoms
